This checklist outlines the necessary steps for terminal waste management, cleaning, and decontamination processes. It is essential to identify the following agencies and personnel for facility inspection before, during, and after terminal cleaning and decontamination: the Ministry of Health or relevant authority, project officer, infection prevention and control (IPC) officer, cleaners, water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) officer, occupational health and safety officer (if available), laundry staff (optional), waste handler, and security guards. The facility must not be reopened for other purposes until the safe completion of the process is documented using the checklist. For psychological reasons, it is recommended to repaint walls and/or refresh furniture, if feasible. Spraying rooms with disinfectants is not recommended, as it is a potentially hazardous practice with no proven disease control benefits, and the disinfectant may not reach all desired surfaces. Spraying may be acceptable outdoors when it is the only feasible option or necessary to disinfect sand or gravel floors. When spraying is used, cleaning with water and detergent to mechanically remove contaminants and organic matter should precede it. After spraying disinfectant, it is necessary to ensure proper distribution on surfaces. Cleaners performing spraying must wear full personal protective equipment (PPE). This checklist is a tool recommended for use by the intended user, and the information collected is not intended for CDC data collection purposes. The CDC does not plan to collect this information. During terminal cleaning and decontamination of Ebola care facilities, cleaners, hygienists, and other personnel must wear full PPE in the red (high-risk) zone for all activities conducted before or during the process. All intact objects and equipment suitable for cleaning and decontamination should be identified and labeled. The clean area should be equipped with a body-sized mirror, a poster outlining steps for donning PPE, a hand hygiene station, and adequate stocks of equipment. Similarly, the area should have a body-sized mirror, a poster on PPE removal steps, a hand hygiene station, decontamination equipment, and a waste bin. All environmental surfaces, including furniture, walls, and doors, must be cleaned. Spills, including blood, body fluids, secretions, or excretions, should be removed by covering them with a rag or paper towel, wiping them up, and placing the waste, rags, or towels into a laundry container for laundering or a waste bucket designated as infectious waste for disposal. A solution containing 5000 ppm available free chlorine or another suitable disinfectant should be used. Rags holding dust must not be shaken out. If septic tanks require desludging, this should be addressed. If oversized or heavy materials need to be transported, appropriate vehicles such as trucks or cranes should be arranged. A sanitary survey of water points used by the Ebola treatment center should be conducted. If the site is dismantled, pipes must be removed to an approved dumping site. Occupational health and safety (OHS) lessons learned and recommendations should be reported. Risks must be assessed, and mitigation measures should be in place to ensure safety during the process.
